Meridian Office Supplies — Weekly Ops Sync (transcript, fictional company, all names invented)
Attendees: Priya (Sales Lead), Dana (Sales Associate), Marcus (Billing Manager), Lena (Sales Director)

Priya: Morning everyone. Let's run through the quote-to-cash flow since we had
a couple of new hires shadow it this week and they had questions.

Dana: Sure. So walking through it end to end — step one, I qualify the lead.
I confirm the company is a real business, get their tax ID, and check they're
not already an existing account in the system. Step two, once qualified I
build the quote in the quoting tool using the current price sheet — line
items, quantities, and the standard tiered pricing. Step three, I send the
draft quote to the customer for a first read before it's finalized, so they
can flag anything before we lock it in. That's the three-step process for
getting a quote out the door.

Priya: Good summary. And after that?

Dana: After qualification and the quote is accepted, I hand the whole file
over to Marcus's team in billing — they take it from there for invoicing and
setting up the payment terms. So Dana hands the file to billing once
qualification and quote sign-off are done.

Marcus: Right, and once it lands with billing we open the account in the
finance system and issue the first invoice within two business days.

Priya: One thing that keeps coming up — discount approvals. Can we restate
the rule for the new hires?

Lena: Yes. Any discount above $2,000 needs written approval from the sales
director before it goes out. That's me. Anything under that, Dana and the
sales team can approve on their own judgment. Anything above $2,000 in
discount value, no exceptions, it has to come to me in writing — an email is
fine, but it has to be in writing, not just a verbal okay in the hallway.

Dana: Got it, that matches what I tell new hires. Discounts above $2,000
always go to Lena first.

Priya: Perfect, let's make sure that's written down somewhere for onboarding.

Marcus: While we're on policy — can we settle the refund policy question?
Priya and I disagree on this one. I think refunds should only be issued
against the original payment method, full stop, no exceptions, because
that's what our processor recommends.

Priya: I don't think that's settled though. I think for repeat customers with
an account in good standing, we should be able to issue store credit instead
of a refund to the original method, especially for international customers
where card refunds take weeks. We've never actually agreed on this — it's
come up three times this quarter and every time we've handled it differently
depending on who picks up the ticket.

Marcus: Right, and I still don't think that's the right call, but I agree we
haven't actually decided as a team. It's genuinely unresolved — we should get
it on the agenda for next week and actually decide one way or the other
instead of everyone guessing.

Priya: Agreed, that one's still open. Let's not pretend we have a policy when
we don't.

Lena: Put it on next week's agenda, I'll make the final call if you two can't
agree beforehand.

Priya: Works for me. Anything else before we wrap?

Dana: Oh — small thing, not really ops-related, but a reminder that it's
Deshawn's week for the ficus schedule, so if you see the office plant looking
dry that's why, he's on it Thursday.

Priya: Noted, thanks Dana. Okay, that's everything for today. Thanks all.
